title.en: Can, can't, could: I can swim

rule.en:
**can** says what someone is able to do, what is allowed, and it asks for things: **I can swim.** (ability) **You can play outside.** (permission) **Can I help?** (asking, offering)

It is the same for every person, with no -s: **I can**, **she can**, **they can** (not *she cans*). The verb after it is the base form, without to: **He can swim.** (not *He can to swim*).

The negative is **can't** (in full: **cannot**): **Meg can't climb trees.** A question puts can first, with no do: **Can you swim?** **Yes, I can.** / **No, I can't.**

**could** is the past (**I could swim when I was five.**) and the more polite way to ask: **Could you open the gate, please?**

can has no future form; use **will be able to**: **I'll be able to come tomorrow.**
rule.sl:
**can** pove, kaj kdo zna ali zmore, kaj je dovoljeno, in z njim prosimo: **I can swim.** (Znam plavati.) **You can play outside.** (Lahko se igraš zunaj.) **Can I help?** (Lahko pomagam?) Slovenski znati, moči, smeti in lahko so v angleščini pogosto vsi **can**.

Za vse osebe je enak, brez -s: **I can**, **she can**, **they can** (ne *she cans*). Glagol za njim je v osnovni obliki, brez to: **He can swim.** (ne *He can to swim*).

Zanikanje je **can't** (v celoti **cannot**): **Meg can't climb trees.** V vprašanju je can prvi, brez do: **Can you swim?** **Yes, I can.** / **No, I can't.**

**could** je preteklik (**I could swim when I was five.** Plavati sem znal že pri petih.) in bolj vljudna prošnja: **Could you open the gate, please?** (Bi lahko odprli vrata, prosim?)

can nima prihodnjika; rabimo **will be able to**: **I'll be able to come tomorrow.** (Jutri bom lahko prišel.)
rule.it:
**can** dice cosa si sa o si riesce a fare, cosa è permesso, e serve per chiedere: **I can swim.** (So nuotare.) **You can play outside.** (Puoi giocare fuori.) **Can I help?** (Posso aiutare?) Potere e sapere (fare qualcosa) in inglese sono spesso tutti e due **can**.

È uguale per tutte le persone, senza -s: **I can**, **she can**, **they can** (non *she cans*). Il verbo dopo è nella forma base, senza to: **He can swim.** (non *He can to swim*).

La negazione è **can't** (per intero **cannot**): **Meg can't climb trees.** Nella domanda can va prima, senza do: **Can you swim?** **Yes, I can.** / **No, I can't.**

**could** è il passato (**I could swim when I was five.** Sapevo già nuotare a cinque anni.) e il modo più gentile di chiedere: **Could you open the gate, please?** (Potrebbe aprire il cancello, per favore?)

can non ha il futuro; si usa **will be able to**: **I'll be able to come tomorrow.** (Domani potrò venire.)
rule.de:
**can** sagt, was jemand kann, was erlaubt ist, und damit bittet man: **I can swim.** (Ich kann schwimmen.) **You can play outside.** (Du darfst draußen spielen.) **Can I help?** (Kann ich helfen?) Können und oft auch dürfen heißen auf Englisch **can**.

Es ist für alle Personen gleich, ohne -s, wie ich kann, er kann: **I can**, **she can**, **they can** (nicht *she cans*). Das Verb danach steht in der Grundform, ohne to (nicht *He can to swim*), und direkt nach can, nicht am Satzende: **He can swim very well.** (Er kann sehr gut schwimmen.)

Die Verneinung ist **can't** (ausgeschrieben **cannot**): **Meg can't climb trees.** In der Frage steht can vorn, ohne do: **Can you swim?** **Yes, I can.** / **No, I can't.**

**could** ist die Vergangenheit (**I could swim when I was five.** Mit fünf konnte ich schon schwimmen.) und die höflichere Bitte: **Could you open the gate, please?** (Könnten Sie bitte das Tor aufmachen?)

can hat kein Futur; man nimmt **will be able to**: **I'll be able to come tomorrow.** (Morgen kann ich kommen.) Nicht *I will can*.

rows: I can swim. She can't swim.
Can I help? Can you help me?
Could you open the gate, please?
Can you swim? — Yes, I can.
I could swim when I was five.
I'll be able to come tomorrow.

examples.en: Can you ride a pony, Harry? — Not yet!
examples.sl: Znaš jahati ponija, Harry? — Še ne!
examples.it: Sai cavalcare un pony, Harry? — Non ancora!
examples.de: Kannst du auf einem Pony reiten, Harry? — Noch nicht!

examples.en: Can I help you, Mr Tyson?
examples.de: Kann ich Ihnen helfen, Herr Tyson?

note.en: Can I …? offers help or asks for something.
note.sl: Can I …? ponudi pomoč ali za kaj prosi.
note.it: Can I …? offre aiuto o chiede qualcosa.
note.de: Can I …? bietet Hilfe an oder bittet um etwas.

examples.en: You can play outside, but you can't go to the beck alone.
examples.sl: Lahko se igraš zunaj, k potoku pa sam ne smeš.
examples.it: Puoi giocare fuori, ma non puoi andare al ruscello da solo.
examples.de: Du darfst draußen spielen, aber nicht allein zum Bach gehen.

note.sl: Dovoljenje: can (lahko, smeš) in can't (ne smeš).

examples.en: Could you open the gate, please?
examples.it: Potrebbe aprire il cancello, per favore?
examples.de: Könnten Sie bitte das Tor aufmachen?

examples.en: Sooty is too small, he can't jump over the wall.
examples.sl: Sooty je premajhen, ne more skočiti čez zid.
examples.it: Sooty è troppo piccolo, non riesce a saltare il muro.
examples.de: Sooty ist zu klein, er kann nicht über die Mauer springen.

examples.en: I could already swim when I was five.
examples.sl: Pri petih letih sem že znal plavati.
examples.it: A cinque anni sapevo già nuotare.
examples.de: Mit fünf konnte ich schon schwimmen.
